10.1145/3728879.title: Are Autonomous Web Agents Good Testers?
10.1145/3728879.reason: Web E2E testing with two open autonomous test agents and 113 tests; no matched traditional script baseline.

arXiv:2603.25226.title: WebTestBench: Evaluating Computer-Use Agents towards End-to-End Automated Web Testing
arXiv:2603.25226.reason: Direct CUA web-testing benchmark; evaluates checklist generation and defect detection rather than CUA-versus-traditional automation.

arXiv:2509.04198.title: Are LLM Agents the New RPA? A Comparative Study with RPA Across Enterprise Workflows
arXiv:2509.04198.reason: Controlled CUA versus UiPath comparison on speed, reliability and development effort, but its workload is enterprise RPA rather than Web software testing.

10.1109/ASEW60602.2023.00028.title: GUI-Based Software Testing: An Automated Approach Using GPT-4 and Selenium WebDriver
10.1109/ASEW60602.2023.00028.reason: Web GUI testing using GPT-4 plus Selenium; compared with monkey testing for branch coverage, not with traditional authored browser automation and not a visual CUA.

10.1007/s11219-026-09767-2.title: Reliable execution of natural language test cases for GUI applications using LLM agents
10.1007/s11219-026-09767-2.reason: Evaluates guarded LLM-agent execution and verdict errors for four natural-language test suites spanning six web apps; no conventional automation or visual-CUA comparison.

arXiv:2605.15281.title: Autonomous Intelligent Agents for Natural-Language-Driven Web Execution with Integrated Security Assurance
arXiv:2605.15281.reason: Preprint reports comparison with manual Selenium authoring but uses DOM-aware script generation, so it is not a screenshot-driven CUA comparison. Full-text methods still require validation.

arXiv:2412.18426.title: GUI Testing Arena: A Unified Benchmark for Advancing Autonomous GUI Testing Agent
arXiv:2412.18426.reason: Open visual-agent testing benchmark over mobile applications; compares MLLMs, not browser automation paradigms.

arXiv:2506.14477.title: GUI-Robust: A Comprehensive Dataset for Testing GUI Agent Robustness in Real-World Anomalies
arXiv:2506.14477.reason: Open GUI-agent dataset with real-world anomaly taxonomy that can inform mutation design; includes web and desktop task traces rather than Web software-test oracles.

arXiv:2401.13919.title: WebVoyager: Building an End-to-End Web Agent with Large Multimodal Models
arXiv:2401.13919.reason: Web navigation comparison of visual and text-only observations; useful for CUA observation ablation, not a testing study.

10.1145/3797115.title: WebTestPilot: Agentic End-to-End Web Testing against Natural Language Specification by Inferring Oracles with Symbolized GUI Elements
10.1145/3797115.reason: Hybrid screenshot-plus-DOM Web testing; its 40-case re-identification sub-study compares against XPath/CSS/Playwright, but it lacks a matched whole-suite CUA-versus-traditional comparison across operational outcomes.

arXiv:2509.05197.title: AI Agents for Web Testing: A Case Study in the Wild
arXiv:2509.05197.reason: Visual agent explores 120 public websites and reports usability issues; no matched conventional testing baseline or regression-suite comparison.

10.1109/ICSME64153.2025.00104.title: XTestGen: Natural Language to Maintainable E2E Test Scripts with LLMs
10.1109/ICSME64153.2025.00104.reason: A tool demonstration that turns natural language into deterministic E2E scripts; valuable hybrid alternative, not a CUA comparison experiment.

arXiv:2607.05031.title: LLM-Based Test Oracles: Source-of-Authority Taxonomy -- A Systematic Literature Review
arXiv:2607.05031.reason: PRISMA SLR of 83 studies; frames oracle authority separately from mechanism and motivates independently grounded fault-detection metrics.

10.1002/smr.2606.title: An empirical study to compare three web test automation approaches: NLP-based, programmable, and capture&replay
10.1002/smr.2606.reason: Matched empirical comparison of NLP-based, programmable and capture-and-replay Web automation with development/evolution cost; no screenshot CUA, a11y-locator arm, independent oracle audit or repeated stochastic CUA runs.

10.1007/s10664-026-10903-6.title: Web element relocalization in evolving web applications: A comparative analysis and extension study
10.1007/s10664-026-10903-6.reason: Public 30-app, >10k-pair benchmark for locator relocalization under UI evolution; strong repair precedent, but no CUA or whole-test comparison.

10.1016/j.jss.2026.112849.title: BEWT: Extended benchmarking for end-to-end web testing
10.1016/j.jss.2026.112849.reason: Shared benchmark and reproducible harness precedent for end-to-end Web testing; exact modality arms, oracle, mutation and reset details require local audit.

10.35784/jcsi.7119.title: A comparative analysis of web application test automation tools
10.35784/jcsi.7119.reason: Empirical Playwright/Cypress/Selenium execution-time, CPU and RAM comparison; no CUA, oracle or evolution study.

10.1016/j.jss.2020.110841.title: An automated model-based approach to repair test suites of evolving web applications
10.1016/j.jss.2020.110841.reason: Empirical Web test-suite repair against Selenium breakages and WATER; informs repair success and effort outcomes, but has no visual/hybrid CUA arm.

10.1016/j.jss.2023.111932.title: Investigating the robustness of locators in template-based Web application testing using a GUI change classification model
10.1016/j.jss.2023.111932.reason: Benchmark of realistic GUI/layout changes and locator strategies; no screenshot CUA or independent three-arm comparison.

arXiv:2606.16650.title: Understanding Automated Web GUI Testing: An Empirical Study Across Exploration Strategies and State Abstractions
arXiv:2606.16650.reason: Compares model-based, RL and LLM exploration/state abstractions over six Web apps using coverage and failure revelation; no authored Playwright baseline or screenshot-only CUA comparison.

10.1145/3735553.title: Large Language Models for Automated Web-Form-Test Generation
10.1145/3735553.reason: Evaluates LLM Web-form test generation over 146 forms in 30 Java applications; DOM/HTML-driven generation, not screenshot CUA versus authored suite.

arXiv:2506.00520.title: Temac: Multi-agent Web GUI testing
arXiv:2506.00520.reason: Multi-agent Web GUI testing over six open-source applications; no conventional authored Playwright arm or independent modality comparison.

arXiv:2504.19237.title: WebRLED: Reinforcement Learning for Web GUI Testing
arXiv:2504.19237.reason: RL Web GUI exploration over 12 open-source apps plus a field study; no screenshot CUA versus deterministic suite comparison.

10.1145/3613904.3642777.title: AXNav: Replaying Accessibility Tests from Natural Language
10.1145/3613904.3642777.reason: Natural-language accessibility replay with pixel-based UI understanding on mobile; informs accessibility oracle terminology but is not Web software testing.

10.1016/j.infsof.2025.107928.title: Investigating the adoption and maintenance of web GUI testing: Insights from GitHub repositories
10.1016/j.infsof.2025.107928.reason: Repository mining across 472 open-source applications and multiple Web testing frameworks; motivates maintenance outcomes but is not a CUA intervention comparison.
